result.final_text:
## What this letter says
Your son was in hospital with Kawasaki disease. The letter says it is resolving.

He was treated with high dose aspirin and IVIG. His fever came back within 12 hours of the first IVIG. The IVIG was repeated twice. After the second IVIG, he had no more fever.

Today his fever and rash have completely gone. He has no conjunctivitis. He has no redness of the mucous membranes.

His echocardiogram was negative.

He is calmer. He is eating and drinking well by mouth.

## What you need to do
1. See his primary doctor in 2 to 3 days.
2. Take him to the cardiology follow-up for an echo in 4 to 6 weeks.
3. Give the medicines as listed below.
4. His activity and food are as he likes (ad-lib).
5. Do not give any live virus vaccine for less than 11 months. This is because of the IVIG.

## Dates and medicines
- Primary doctor: in 2 to 3 days.
- Cardiology with echo: in 4 to 6 weeks.
- Aspirin, high dose: 340 milligrams every 6 hours, for 1 day. This is new.
- Aspirin, low dose: 40 milligrams once a day, for 14 days. This is new. It is for after the 1 day of high dose.
- Prevacid: 15 milligrams by mouth, once a day. This is new. It protects his stomach and bowel (GI) from the aspirin.
- The letter does not give the exact start date for the aspirin.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When exactly should the aspirin start, and when do the 14 days begin?
- The letter says no vaccines "in less than 11 months". Does that mean 11 months from now?
- What is Kawasaki disease?
- What will the echo at cardiology check?

## When to get urgent help
If he gets any rashes or any fevers, go to the primary care doctor as soon as possible.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
